deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can delete or abandon the resource. Preventing unintended destruction can help preserve infrastructure and associated security controls.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: This is descriptive metadata only and does not directly affect the security behaviour or configuration of the resource.

instance.description:
The Compute instance VM handling traffic for this target instance.
Accepts the instance self-link, relative path
(e.g. 'projects/project/zones/zone/instances/instance') or name. If
name is given, the zone will default to the given zone or
the provider-default zone and the project will default to the
provider-level project.
instance.rationale: This identifies or references the specific Compute instance used by the target instance. Resource references are team-specific and should not be constrained by a general platform-wide security policy.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The resource name is an identifier and does not directly control the security behaviour of the target instance.

nat_policy.description:
NAT option controlling how IPs are NAT'ed to the instance.
Currently only NO_NAT (default value) is supported. Default value: "NO_NAT" Possible values: ["NO_NAT"]
nat_policy.rationale: Although this describes NAT behaviour, the only supported value is NO_NAT. There is therefore no configurable security choice that can be meaningfully constrained by a platform-wide policy.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This identifies the project containing the resource. Project identifiers are team-specific scope references and cannot be generalised into a platform-wide security policy.

zone.description: URL of the zone where the target instance resides.
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).
